newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan approves Big Three Banks' privatisation.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan approves Big Three Banks' privatisation.

text.p: The Taiwan Provincial Assembly had given final approval on the long-awaited privatisation scheme on the "big three" state-run commercial banks, planning to complete privatisation within 12-18 months, officials said on Friday.
The three are Chang Hwa Bank, First Commercial Bank and Hua Nan Bank.
"The Taiwan Provincial Assembly on Thursday gave the final nod, and we plan to complete privatisation of the big three banks between 12 to 18 months," a provincial government official told Reuters.
The government decided to release 15.9 percent of First Commercial's shares, 7.5 percent of Huan Nan's and 4.65 percent of Chang Hwa's, he said by telephone.
After the share sale, government holdings would fall to 46 percent of First Commercial, 45 percent of Hua Nan and 37.83 percent of Chang Hwa, the official said.
The Provincial Assembly on Thursday abolished its 1989 decision not to let state stakes in the Big Three fall below 51 percent.

"It's good after privatisation. The three banks' operational efficiency should improve significantly, but it's bad that the huge new share supplies may dampen prices," said National Securities manager Allen Huang.
